text.name: Safe DLL search
text.titlePass: Programs load their libraries from safe places first
text.titleFail: Programs look for libraries in the current folder first
text.why: With safe search off, a program opened from a folder with a planted library loads the attacker's code instead of its own.
fix: Tell IT: the value SafeDllSearchMode shown in the details must be 1 or absent.

text.name: Drivers loaded at start-up
text.titlePass: Windows does not load drivers known to be bad at start-up
text.titleFail: Windows loads every driver at start-up, even known bad ones
text.why: The antivirus rates each driver before Windows starts. Loading the ones it rates as bad gives malware control before anything can stop it.
fix: Tell IT: the policy is "Boot-Start Driver Initialization Policy" under System > Early Launch Antimalware.
It must not be set to "All".

labels.3: Good, unknown and bad but needed to start

absent.found: Not configured (Windows default: good, unknown and bad but needed to start)

text.name: Exception chain protection (SEHOP)
text.titlePass: Exception chain protection is switched on
text.titleFail: Exception chain protection is not switched on
text.why: SEHOP blocks an old way of taking over 32-bit programs through their error handling. Microsoft's baseline switches it on for all programs.
fix: Tell IT: the value DisableExceptionChainValidation shown in the details must be 0.

text.name: Right to debug programs
text.titlePass: Only administrators may debug other programs
text.titleFail: Others than administrators may debug other programs
text.why: Whoever may debug any program can read its memory, passwords included, and take over Windows itself.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Debug programs and leave only Administrators.

text.name: Right to connect over the network
text.titlePass: Only administrators and remote users may connect to this PC
text.titleFail: Everyone may connect to this PC over the network
text.why: This right decides who may reach shared folders and services on this PC at all. Windows gives it to everyone by default.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is User Rights Assignment > Access this computer from the network: Administrators and Remote Desktop Users only.

userRight.item: Access this computer from the network

text.name: Right to act as the operating system
text.titlePass: No account may act as part of the operating system
text.titleFail: An account may act as part of the operating system
text.why: This right lets a program become any user without a password. Windows needs no account to hold it.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Act as part of the operating system.
Remove every account.

userRight.item: Act as part of the operating system

text.name: Right to create sign-in tokens
text.titlePass: No account may make its own sign-in tokens
text.titleFail: An account may make its own sign-in tokens
text.why: With this right a program can give itself any rights at all. Only Windows itself needs it.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Create a token object.
Remove every account.

text.name: Right to read saved passwords
text.titlePass: No account may read saved passwords as a trusted caller
text.titleFail: An account may read saved passwords as a trusted caller
text.why: Windows uses this right to restore saved passwords from a backup. Held by an account, it opens every stored sign-in.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller.
Remove every account.

userRight.item: Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller

text.name: Right to load drivers
text.why: A driver runs inside Windows itself, without limits. Loading one is as good as full control.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Load and unload device drivers.
Leave only Administrators.

text.name: Right to take ownership
text.titlePass: Only administrators may take ownership of files
text.titleFail: Other accounts may take ownership of files
text.why: Taking ownership of a file or setting lets the new owner change who may use it, past every other protection.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Take ownership of files or other objects.
Leave only Administrators.

userRight.item: Take ownership of files or other objects

text.name: Right to back up files
text.titlePass: Only administrators and backup operators may back up files
text.titleFail: Other accounts may read every file through backup rights
text.why: The backup right reads any file whatever its permissions, the password database included.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Back up files and directories.
Leave only Administrators and Backup Operators.

text.name: Right to restore files
text.titlePass: Only administrators and backup operators may restore files
text.titleFail: Other accounts may overwrite any file through restore rights
text.why: The restore right writes any file whatever its permissions, Windows' own programs included.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Restore files and directories.
Leave only Administrators and Backup Operators.

text.name: Right to change firmware settings
text.titlePass: Only administrators may change firmware settings
text.titleFail: Other accounts may change firmware settings
text.why: Firmware settings decide how the PC starts. Changing them can weaken the protections that run before Windows does.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Modify firmware environment values.
Leave only Administrators.

text.name: Right to manage the security log
text.titlePass: Only administrators may manage the security log
text.titleFail: Other accounts may manage the security log
text.why: This right reads and clears the security log, the record of sign-ins and changes. An intruder clears it to hide.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Manage auditing and security log.
Leave only Administrators.
